correctness.rationale: Reconstructs the stationary vector transform from two Markov generator equations, its positive subordinator Lévy density, the unique Bessel radial Lévy density and polar class-L criterion. The Bessel quotient is <2 for all radii and converges to 2 as r decreases to zero for every d>=2, proving iff alpha>=2 and equality. Radial integration proves the nonnegative compound-Poisson driver has rate alpha and reconstructs the OU invariant measure. The common-switch and scalar-drift restrictions are explicit. The standalone package checker passed 393 finite diagnostics, not an infinite proof.

evidence: Sato (2001) establishes inheritance of self-decomposability from an SD subordinator to Brownian subordination, a sufficient condition.

Buchmann–Lu–Madan (2017/2019) consider Brownian motions weakly subordinated by Thorin subordinators; the source subordinator multiplier (1+alpha/2)e^{-alpha t}-e^{-2alpha t} is not completely monotone as t varies, and is not a Thorin multiplier.
No inspected theorem supplies the physical-model-specific necessity or the interval of coordinatewise class-L without joint class-L.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The subordinator is self-decomposable exactly when alpha>=2 by differentiating its t-times-Lévy-density. Classical inheritance supplies the upper-regime sufficiency but does not prove that the multidimensional subordinated law fails class L below alpha=2, nor the explicit positive finite-rate vector driver or strict scalar-projection gap. The Bessel-polar proof supplies those missing consequences. A full-text stronger converse elsewhere remains a residual risk.
